source.title: Letting the neural code speak: Automated characterization of monkey visual neurons through human language
source.authors: Vedang Lad; Katrin Franke; T. Shaham; Surya Ganguli; A. Tolias; Sophia Sanborn; Nikos Karantzas

record.tranche_reason: The study measures cross-space representational alignment and explicitly characterizes it as partial, with differences across representational spaces and cortical areas. It does not test alignment growth with model scale or capability.
record.gate_note: The RSA results directly bear on partial alignment (V7). The study does not sweep model size or capability, compare independently trained AI models, or test whether vision-language alignment rises as both models improve. The reported neuron-verification rates and random-image control concern semantic descriptions of neural selectivity, not convergence, so they are not rows here.
record.test_reason: The study measures preservation of neuron-to-neuron selectivity geometry across a biological-neuron interpretation pipeline. It does not test convergence among independently trained models, growth of vision-language alignment with capability, or explanations of incomplete model convergence. Its connection to the Platonic hypothesis is an analogy. Correlations below one across these pipeline stages do not by themselves test V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that natural language provides verifiable descriptions of most sampled neurons' selectivity and partially preserves population selectivity geometry. Visual embeddings align more strongly with predicted neural activity than language embeddings; the generated-image loop preserves geometry better in V4 than V1. Verification remains in silico and conditional on an ImageNet-centered pipeline; shared inductive biases are a limitation, not an established explanation of the RSA results.
record.recipe_differences: Uses RSA to compare neural, visual, and language representational spaces for macaque V1/V4; does not measure scale-related convergence among independently trained models or compare model capabilities.
record.method_sensitivity: Alignment magnitudes differ across representational-space pairs and cortical areas; V1 loop closure is weaker than V4. Only one RSA measure and one held-out construction are reported.

fits_no_version.finding: All 30 cross-space RSA correlations exceed their permutation nulls: r = 0.102–0.674 in V1 and 0.192–0.670 in V4. These describe neuron-to-neuron geometry across representations of selected activating stimuli. Original-to-generated digital-twin response geometry is retained more strongly in V4 (0.491) than V1 (0.249).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Language descriptions partially preserve the selectivity geometry of macaque visual-neuron digital twins, and hypothesis-conditioned image generation recovers some geometry lost through linguistic compression.

record.problems: The RSA analysis uses one measure and selected ImageNet most-activating stimuli, with no alternate metric or out-of-distribution input test. The authors flag overlapping ImageNet-related training distributions and shared inductive biases; verification is against digital twins rather than direct neural recordings. The study does not test scale or capability.
record.rows_left_out: No RSA results left out. Verification success percentages and random-image augmentation controls in Table 1 were excluded because they assess semantic hypothesis verification, not representational convergence.

untested.parts: Alignment growth with model scale or capability across independently trained models.
Whether alignment of paired image-caption representations increases as vision and language models improve.
Shared features or subspaces across independently initialized networks of the same architecture.
Interchangeability through simple mappings, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired alignment; generative reconstruction does not establish these.
Recurrence of the same interpretable features or circuits across models.
Sensitivity of convergence to similarity metrics, metric settings, input distributions, or out-of-distribution evaluation.

Persistent incomplete convergence or plateaus across models, and causal explanations involving shared training data or objectives. The shared-bias discussion concerns verification performance and proposes future controls.

record.verdict_notes: Table 2 confirms the extracted correlations, p-values, and null thresholds. The replacement states concern inability to determine a claim-version effect, not absence of the reported RSA correspondence. Differences across representational spaces or cortical areas do not establish V6 metric dependence. Partial pipeline fidelity also cannot justify a limits_scope verdict on V7, whose stated prediction already includes partial alignment.

versions.untested_parts: Model scale, capability, and alignment among independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, and data.
No test of whether paired image-caption vision-language alignment increases as both models improve.
No comparison of same-architecture networks trained from different initializations or their shared features/subspaces.
No test of mappings, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired alignment between models.
No test of recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.
Uses RSA and a particular set of activating images, but does not vary similarity measures, their settings, or input distributions to test metric or data dependence.

Does not establish a plateau, test whether shared training data or objectives explain alignment, or distinguish those explanations from a common model of reality. Its shared-inductive-bias caveat concerns the verification pipeline, not a causal test of RSA alignment.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: All reported cross-space RSA pairs in V1 and V4
reader_labels.reason: All listed correlations exceed their permutation-null thresholds, indicating shared but partial geometric alignment rather than chance correspondence (V1-RSA-01–15; V4-RSA-01–15).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Language-related alignments and generated-image loop closure, especially V1
reader_labels.reason: Alignment varies by representational space and area: neural activity aligns more strongly with image embeddings than with hypothesis embeddings, and neural-to-generated-response alignment is lower in V1 than V4 (V1-RSA-06, V1-RSA-12, V4-RSA-06, V4-RSA-12).
